newsitem.title: USA: Florida stock promoter pleads guilty.
newsitem.headline: Florida stock promoter pleads guilty.

text.p: A Florida stock promoter pleaded guilty to securities fraud, money laundering and other charges accusing him of making illegal payments to securities and stock promoters, federal prosecutors said Tuesday.
Richard Mallion, 31, pleaded guilty to a five-count criminal information before U.S. District Judge Denny Chin on Thursday. The plea was unsealed in court Tuesday.
Mallion faces up to 40 years in prison and millions of dollars in fines, prosecutors said. Sentencing was set for Dec. 15.
Mallion admitted that from 1993 to 1996, he conspired to
make unlawful and secret payments of cash and stock to securities brokers and stock promoters. Authorities did not give Mallion's hometown, nor say how much money was involved.
The charges stem from an undercover FBI investigation into illegal payments by the brokers and stock promoters.

In addition to securities fraud and money laundering, Mallion pleaded guilty to conspiracy and criminal contempt charges in the criminal information, prosecutors said. A criminal information is similar to an indictment but is issued by prosecutors instead of a grand jury.
Two of the five counts are the result of an unrelated scheme in which Mallion, 31, defrauded investors in Chartbreaker, a company purportedly in the business of renting compact discs.
Mallion also pleaded guilty to a second conspiracy count to commit securities, mail and wire fraud involving Chartbreaker.
Prosecutors said FBI agents posed as unscrupulous stockbrokers and accepted bribes for selling securities to their customers in 23 companies.

According to the court document, Mallion made more than 30 payments to undercover FBI agents to induce customers to buy stock. These payments involved transfers of cash from Canada to the United States.
